core_obligations: Set h = g o f and record the identification of the pullback of the structure sheaf (proof line 3958).
Use the pullback statement to write f^{-1}L_g as a cotangent complex of sheaves of rings and note its flatness (proof lines 3959-3961).
Recognize the claimed triangle as the one supplied by the sheaf-theoretic triangle lemma for the three sheaves of rings (proof lines 3962-3966).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for morphisms of ringed topoi f and g, there is a canonical distinguished triangle Lf^*L_g -> L_{g o f} -> L_f -> Lf^*L_g[1] in D(O_1) (source lines 3944-3955). The proof sets h = g o f and uses the pullback statement to identify f^{-1}L_g with the cotangent complex of the map of sheaves of rings h^{-1}O_3 -> f^{-1}O_2, noting that this is a complex of flat f^{-1}O_2-modules; the triangle in question is then the triangle of the sheaf-theoretic triangle lemma for the three sheaves of rings involved.
